rounds.text: Modison Ltd trades at a compelling valuation of 9.16x P/E, which is dramatically lower than the sector benchmark of 21.1x [E1, E6]. This low multiple stands in stark contrast to the company's exceptional profitability metrics, featuring an ROE of 32.0% and an ROCE of 31.0%, both drastically outperforming sector benchmarks of 11.35% and 12.93% respectively [E9, E10, E13]. Fundamental growth has been extraordinary across multiple time horizons, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 83% over 3 years and an astonishing 269% over the trailing twelve months [E20, E21]. Operational efficiency has also expanded significantly, with operating margins rising by 9 percentage points to 17% in the TTM period compared to three years prior [E29]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models suggest a massive intrinsic value of Rs 1417 per share against a market price of ₹ 330, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 76.7% [E43, E44]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -64 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a weak cash conversion ratio of -0.88x [E33, E34].

Despite headline growth figures, Modison Ltd exhibits severe fundamental cracks centered on a complete collapse in cash generation. Operating cash flow for March 2026 plunged to negative Rs 64 Cr, resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -0.88x against reported profit, alongside a negative free cash flow of Rs 79 Cr [E33, E34, E35]. This cash burn is accompanied by rising financial obligations as total borrowings climbed to Rs 222 Cr in September 2026, up from Rs 174 Cr a year prior [E38]. Conceded: the company displays high trailing returns on equity and capital employed alongside multi-year compounding in sales and profit [E13, E16, E20]. However, margin pressures are already materializing with quarterly operating margins contracting by 2 percentage points year-over-year to 11% in September 2026 [E30], while the screening engine flags that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E65].

Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative Rs 64 Cr and borrowings rose to Rs 222 Cr in September 2026 [E34, E38]. However, this short-term cash burn coincides directly with a 133.3% surge in capital work-in-progress up to Rs 7 Cr, confirming an active capex build-up phase geared toward future growth [E39]. The market is overly penalising these temporary outlays while completely ignoring Modison's exceptional structural profitability, evidenced by an ROE of 32.0% and an ROCE of 31.0% [E12, E13]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on a single quarter's 2 percentage point margin contraction [E30] overlooks the massive broader expansion where operating margins climbed 9 percentage points over three years to 17% in the TTM [E29]. Finally, the claim of decelerating earnings [E65] is contradicted by explosive trailing momentum, including an 85% TTM sales growth and a 269% TTM profit growth [E17, E21], supported by robust domestic and global demand for high and low voltage products [E74].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 85% and profit growth hit 269% [E17, E21]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash burn as merely a sign of growth ignores the sheer scale of the deterioration, with operating cash flow plunging to negative Rs 64 Cr and free cash flow dropping to negative Rs 79 Cr for March 2026 [E34, E35], resulting in a dismal cash conversion of -0.88x [E33]. Furthermore, this capital expenditure surge is accompanied by an alarming accumulation of debt, with total borrowings expanding to Rs 222 Cr by September 2026 compared to Rs 174 Cr a year prior [E38]. While the bull points to a three-year margin expansion, the more recent evidence exposes clear operational fragility, including an inconsistent yearly and quarterly margin trend [E31, E32] alongside a sequential 2 percentage point contraction in quarterly operating margin as of September 2026 [E30]. Finally, the screen engine itself explicitly flags earnings growth as decelerating [E65], directly undermining the notion that explosive trailing momentum can be extrapolated into the future without substantial financial strain.

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -64 Cr and free cash flow was Rs -79 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35], leading to a negative cash conversion of -0.88x [E33]. However, this cash drain occurs during a capital expenditure build-up phase where CWIP expanded by 133.3% to Rs 7 Cr [E39], signaling heavy growth spend underway rather than operational failure. The bear's concern over rising borrowings to Rs 222 Cr [E38] is mitigated by a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.69x [E36] and stellar returns on capital, with ROCE reaching 30.43% to 31.0% and ROE hitting up to 35.14% [E10, E12, E9]. Conceded: quarterly operating margin contracted by 2 percentage points to 11% in September 2026 [E30] and trends are flagged as inconsistent [E31, E32], but the TTM operating margin still reflects a massive multi-year structural expansion of +9 percentage points against three years earlier [E29]. Finally, while earnings growth deceleration is flagged [E65], the reverse DCF reveals that today's price of ₹ 330 already prices in a negative -2.2% growth rate against a base case assumption of 18.0% [E45, E2], leaving a massive margin of safety of 76.7% based on a DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 1417 [E43, E44].

Conceded: the reverse DCF indicates the market price of ₹330 prices in a negative -2.2% growth rate compared to an 18.0% base case [E45, E2]. However, the bull's dismissal of the severe cash drain as a mere capex build-up phase ignores that operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs 64 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 79 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.88x [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, while the bull minimizes the rising borrowings to Rs 222 Cr in September 2026 [E38], this debt expansion accompanies an inconsistent operating margin trend [E31, E32] and a contraction to 11% in September 2026 [E30]. Conceded: the TTM operating margin shows multi-year expansion [E29], but the recent quarterly compression demonstrates that operational momentum is faltering [E30]. Finally, the stock's high annualised volatility of 58.6% [E52] and historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -48.8% [E51] expose investors to extreme downside risk that a theoretical intrinsic value model fails to mitigate.
